content_calendar.title: Built a tool that audits your site the same way your CI audits your code — dogfooding it on our own site right now (71/100, and our AI Readiness is 1%)

content_calendar.title: Cloudflare's Sep 15 default can block Googlebot on ad-supported pages, because Googlebot is a 'mixed-use' crawler — free check for whether it hit you
content_calendar.body:
Since 2026-09-15 Cloudflare blocks AI Training and Agent crawlers by default on ad-supported pages. It applies to new domains, new sites on existing accounts, and free-tier accounts that haven't changed the setting — existing paid customers were notified and can opt out in zone security settings.

The part worth knowing: Googlebot is *mixed-use*. It crawls for Search and for AI training in one bot, and mixed-use crawlers are treated under whichever rule is most restrictive. So a site blocking Training crawlers — including via the legacy "Block AI Bots" toggle — can also be blocking Googlebot on its ad-supported pages unless it explicitly opts out.

I built a free check for this into RankCLI (`npx @rankcli/mcp-server`, no signup, runs locally in Claude Code/Cursor/whatever) alongside the usual technical SEO — Core Web Vitals, structured data, security headers. It reports which of GPTBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot/Googlebot can actually reach you.

Curious whether anyone here has actually seen impressions drop since the 15th.

content_calendar.title: The data behind 'AI SEO': being crawled isn't the win, being cited is (35%/91% more clicks when you are)
content_calendar.body: Google's own numbers: organic CTR on AI-Overview queries has fallen from ~1.8% to under 1% since mid-2024, but brands actually cited in an AI answer get 35% more organic clicks and 91% more paid clicks than uncited brands, even when both rank the same underlying position. That gap is the whole thesis behind a CI-native SEO/GEO tool I built (RankCLI) — treating AI-citation readiness as a lint target instead of a marketing metric. Wrote up the full research behind the positioning if anyone wants the source data, otherwise happy to talk shop on the GEO checks specifically.
